papers.title: On Microstructure Evolution and Mechanical Behavior of Near Equiatomic Nickel Titanium (NiTi) Alloys Fabricated by Laser Deposition of Elemental Powders
papers.abstract: Elementary powder of nickel (Ni) and titanium (Ti) were deposited on the surface of a Ti-6Al-4V alloy substrate by direct laser deposition. By varying laser parameters such as power and scan speed, we investigated how these factors affect phase formation, hardness, elastic modulus, and elastic recovery. Microstructural analysis revealed dendritic structure in most specimens, with variations in the formation of second phase precipitates, such as TiNi2 and TiNi3, depending on the processing conditions. Specimens processed with higher laser energy had fewer dendritic structures. A nanoindentation test was carried out to assess the hardness and elastic recovery of the specimens, showing differences in mechanical properties linked to the processing parameters, and it revealed that specimens processed with higher laser energy exhibited superior mechanical properties, with a recovery index reaching 30% in some cases that includes laser power of 1.25 Kw and scan speed of 1.5 m/min. When the optimized laser parameters were used, more homogeneous phases were formed, enhancing both hardness and elasticity. This study shows that direct laser deposition can be adjusted to improve the performance of NiTi alloys for applications that need high strength and elasticity.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文主要研究NiTi合金而非Ti-6Al-4V，仅以Ti-6Al-4V为基板，对Ti-6Al-4V的力学与疲劳性能无贡献。
llm.why_not_core: Does not investigate Ti-6Al-4V mechanical or fatigue performance; instead focuses on near-equiatomic NiTi alloy fabricated by laser deposition of elemental powders on a Ti-6Al-4V substrate.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究激光沉积工艺参数对NiTi合金相形成及力学性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 在Ti-6Al-4V基板上通过直接激光沉积Ni和Ti元素粉末，改变激光功率和扫描速度。
summary_zh.result: 高激光能量试样获得更均匀组织，硬度与弹性回复率提升，最大回复指数达30%。
summary_zh.validation: 纳米压痕测试评估硬度、弹性模量和弹性回复。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to understand how laser processing parameters affect phase formation and mechanical properties of NiTi alloys fabricated by direct laser deposition of elemental powders.
summary_en.method: Nickel and titanium elemental powders were laser-deposited onto a Ti-6Al-4V substrate with varying laser power and scan speed to fabricate NiTi alloy specimens.
summary_en.result: Higher laser energy led to more homogeneous phase formation and superior mechanical properties, with elastic recovery index reaching up to 30%.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were evaluated via nanoindentation testing for hardness, elastic modulus, and elastic recovery.
